newsitem.title: USA: NBA-OLAJUWON LEADS ROCKETS PAST KINGS.
newsitem.headline: NBA-OLAJUWON LEADS ROCKETS PAST KINGS.

text.p: Hakeem Olajuwon scored 26 points and Randy Livingston had nine in a decisive 22-7 second-half run, leading the Houston Rockets to their third win of the season over the Sacramento Kings, 89-80 Thursday.
Charles Barkley had 16 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists before leaving late in the third qaurter with a sprained right ankle. He will miss Friday's game at Dallas.
"The only thing good tonight is we won the game," Barkley said. "Tomorrow is going to be tough. We've just got to keep the finger in the dyke until we get some guys healthy."

In Atlanta, Christian Laettner scored eight of his 22 points in a 12-0 run that opened the second half as the Atlanta Hawks took the lead for good on the way to a 78-67 victory over the Orlando Magic.
Laettner pulled down 13 rebounds and Steve Smith dished out a season high 10 assists as the Hawks picked up their eighth straight win and 15th consecutive home victory.
In Boston, Tim Hardaway had 22 points and 13 assists and hit a key three-pointer with 83 seconds remaining as the Miami Heat held off the Boston Celtics, 102-94.

Alonzo Mourning added 20 points and nine rebounds and P.J. Brown contributed 14 and 14 for Miami, which has won three of its last four games. The victory moves the Heat into a first-place tie with New York in the Atlantic Division.
"It was a wild game, we knew they were going to play hard and trap," Miami coach Pat Riley said. "For the most part we handled the ball pretty well."
Miami used a 23-4 first-quarter run to take the lead for good.
In Denver, Rickey Pierce made a 10-footer with three seconds left in overtime as the Denver Nuggets stopped a five-game losing streak with an 88-87 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers.
LaPhonso Ellis scored 27 points and Bryant Stith 20 for the Nuggets, who won for just the second time in their last 11 games.
Terrell Brandon had a chance to win the game for Cleveland but his jumper from just right of the free-throw line hit the rim at the buzzer.
At Utah, Karl Malone had 28 points and 11 rebounds and John Stockton added 12 and nine assists as the Utah Jazz won their fifth straight home game, defeating the Phoenix Suns, 95-91.
Jeff Hornacek added 13 as the Jazz, who own the league's third-best home record at 17-2, survived a late run by the Suns.
Kevin Johnson led Phoenix with 21 points and 12 assists while Ceballos added 16 points and 12 rebounds.

In Los Angeles, Isaiah Rider scored 30 points and Clifford Robinson added 18 as the Portland Trail Blazers raced to an early lead and snapped the Los Angeles Lakers' 12-game home-winning streak, 102-98.
Portland, which has won seven of its last eight games, built an 18-point halftime lead and hung on in the second half. Gary Trent added 17 points and eight rebounds for the Trail Blazers.
